title: Redstone descriptor
description: The projection of a Build, a Deployment or a carrier exception, a failed build's or a service's, to data (spec §13.9, D-432, D-434, D-467, D-468). Version 1.0. The writer is `descriptor` in src/descriptor.jl; this file is the shape of record, strict about the writer's output: every object closes with additionalProperties false, and a field that does not apply is omitted, never null. The design record is RedstoneInspector.jl/design/descriptor_design.md. Until the first release the format stays at version 1.0 and changes freely, the schema requiring each section it gains (D-467). `name` is optional, a label for the model that a writer outside the core supplies; `descriptor` never writes it.

FormatVersion.description: The format's own version, independent of Redstone's. A minor bump only adds fields; a major bump may break readers.

DeploymentBody.description: The deployment's body, flat in the order of the Deployment's fields (D-467): the build body whole; the frame period, the base tick and the step bound `h_max`, resolved, each exact; the step floor `h_min`, present only when set; the algorithm; the four budgets; the schedule; and the deployment's own warnings, each a Diagnostic, an empty array when none. A client derives the hyperperiod and the steps per frame, and each schedule row's Δt as D times `dt_base`.

Algorithm.description: The integration method: `text`, what the token's show prints, and `proposes`, whether the method proposes its steps' lengths, which decides whether the steps per frame are a count or a range.

ScheduleSection.description: The Schedule's projection (D-467). `anchors` holds each anchor's counts in base ticks, `D` = dt/dt_base and `phi` = tau/dt_base, in the order of the structure's `anchors`; `rows` one row per discrete primitive in walk order; `scopes` one row per rate scope, in the order of the structure's `scopes`. A row carries no anchor, which its node's timing holds, no rate chain and no Δt.

BuildBody.description: The build's body, one section per artifact, `structure` projects the Structure, `outputs` the Outputs and `events` the Events, and the warnings the build kept, each a Diagnostic, an empty array when none.

FailureBody.description: A carrier exception's body (D-434). `policy` is the carrier's type parameter read out: `fail-fast` lists the one diagnostic that stopped the build, nothing else having been gathered; `collected` lists everything the step found. `structure` is present only when the throw left the build's door past the structure step, and is then the complete Structure, so a client draws the whole model with the error marked on it; without it, the diagnostics are a list. `warnings` are the carrier's: a build's warnings so far, none on a service's.

Diagnostic.description: A diagnostic as its rendering plus the marks a drawing needs, never its payload (§13.9, D-434). `kind` is the diagnostic's type name, Appendix C's closed set; `severity` is `error` or `warning`; `path` is the component the diagnostic is attributed to, "" for the root; `message` is the text `showerror` renders, a UserCodeFraming's cause on its second line. The optional fields are written by the kinds whose payload holds the fact: `function` is the user method at fault for the probe-chain kinds (UserCodeFraming, ConformanceFailure, DeadStage, UndeclaredReturnField); `marks` holds the ports and wires the kind names beyond its path (UnconnectedInput's and TwoProducers' consumer port; WireTypeMismatch's and WalkingFaceAtFrozenEntry's consumer port and producer-to-consumer wire); `cycle` is AlgebraicCycle's cluster.

Marks.description: Where the overlay draws beyond the node `path` names: port squares as endpoints, and wires as endpoint pairs, declared endpoints as the diagnostic's payload spells them.

Cycle.description: An AlgebraicCycle's cluster (§13.8): `members` are component paths in the order the diagnostic lists them; `wires` the cluster's own wires as terminal pairs, primitive output to primitive input; `classification`, `real` or `artificial`, is absent when a member's evaluation threw; `dead` lists every hop the trace found unrouted; `traced` records each member's tracing mode.

DeadHop.description: A hop the trace found unrouted: the member, the input face entering it and the output port that does not route that face.

StructureSection.description: The Structure's projection: every component as a node in walk order, the root inputs typed with their pin, the anchors, the keyed rate scopes, the grid report derived from the anchors, and one row per type.

Node.description: One component of the walk, keyed by its path. `class` says which of the two shapes the node takes.

NodeIdentity.description: The fields both classes share. `path` is the full path, "" for the root. `field` is the field that contributed the node to its parent and `key`, present for a container element alone, its key within the container, a string even when the container is a vector; the root has neither. No `key` is a component field; a `key` with the path's last segment `field/key` is a keyed container; a `key` equal to the last segment is a name-transparent container. `type` is the qualified base name, parent module and all, the key into the `types` table; `alias`, present when a `const` of the type's own module binds a parameterization of it, is the qualified name of the most specific such binding, `Redstone.Library.SumJunction` for a `Junction` at `+`, the label and icon key ahead of `type`; `signature` the full printed concrete type, display text as the REPL prints it.

AssemblyNode.description: An assembly node carries its level's wires verbatim and name-only faces. No tier, no timing.

PrimitiveFace.description: A primitive's face: its name, the declared type as printed (display text), the kind marker, and whether the declaration was wrapped in Pinned.

RootInput.description: A root input: a primitive face's fields, its type the one the wire pass fixed, and `pinned`, the fan-out meet's (D-168, D-468): true when some consumer's entry refuses the type walked to a Dual. `pinned_by` lists those consumers as endpoints, an empty array when none; a discrete consumer pins by tier and a continuous one by declaration, which its node's tier tells.

AssemblyFace.description: An assembly's face: its name alone, as an object so a later bump can add fields.

KindMarker.description: What a face's type is, for a client with no Julia: the first row of §13.9's table that matches the declared type. `struct` is a value the leaf walk opens, an isbits struct, NamedTuple or tuple, with its field names (a tuple's are its positions); a handle, a function, a string, a static array of free size, an abstract or Any declaration is opaque.

Wire.description: One wire of an assembly's level, producer to consumer, verbatim from the level row. A boundary face is spelled with the level's own path, and a root input is a producer at path "". A consumer has one producer and an input entry fanning out is one wire per target, so `to` is unique within a level and keys the wire.

Timing.description: The anchor a primitive or a scope hangs from (0 the base grid), and its divisor `D` and its phase `phi` in that anchor's ticks.

RateLink.description: One `sample_times` link of a primitive's chain, outermost first, as the component row holds it: `scope`, the declaring assembly's path, "" for the root; `key`, the key as written, a container's bare field name included; and the entry, a Relative's `D` and `phi` or an Absolute's `dt` and `tau`. The timing alone does not determine the chain: an explicit Relative(1) changes no timing.

Anchor.description: One Absolute anchor, numbered from 1 by position; anchor 0, the base grid, has no row. `scope` is the declaring assembly's path, "" for the root.

Scope.description: One keyed rate scope: the assembly whose sample_times names the key, and the scope's own timing.

Grid.description: The grid report as data (§9.2, D-466, D-467), derived from the anchors. `admissible` is the coarsest admissible Δt_base, gcd(pool), absent when there are no anchors. `pool` lists the constraint entries, every anchor's period then every nonzero offset, in anchor order. `primes` lists each prime power of the grid's denominator. Every stored position counts from 1.

PoolEntry.description: One pool entry: `anchor`, the anchor's position in `anchors` from 1, whose row holds the entry's value, scope and key; `kind`, its period or its offset; `factor`, the leave-one-out refinement factor gcd(pool without it)/gcd(pool); and `alternatives`, present on a driving offset that has some, the nearest offsets the rest of the pool supports.

PrimeRow.description: One prime power of the grid's denominator: `prime`, `power` and `suppliers`, the positions in `pool` from 1 of the entries whose denominators it divides. `unfactored`, present only when true, marks a cofactor the trial division left whole, which may be composite; its suppliers are the entries whose denominators share a factor with it.

TypeRow.description: One row per qualified base name: the docstring as Markdown source, absent when the type has none, and the locations of the declaration methods the type defines.

Parameter.description: One inert field of an instance as display text: repr under :compact and :limit, cut at 80 characters with an ellipsis. A NamedTuple field with fields is opened into one entry per field, named by the dotted path, a nested NamedTuple in turn; an empty one keeps its entry.

OutputsSection.description: The Outputs' projection: the execution order as primitive paths, and per primitive the port names each stage produces.

EventsSection.description: The Events' projection (D-467): one row per primitive in walk order, as the artifact holds them, so a position addresses a row here and in the outputs' `components` alike.

ComponentEvents.description: A primitive's events in declaration order, which is their priority order, and the event bundle's field names; both empty for a primitive that declares none.
